headlines.title: McDonald’s (MCD) Stock May Trade Near Fair Value Following Dividend Raise
headlines.summary: McDonald's stock has fallen about 20% year to date, even as the fast food giant raises its dividend and refreshes leadership in its key U.S. business. That puts fresh focus on a simple question for investors: Is the current share price in line with what the restaurant chain's cash flows can support over time? The roughly 20% year to date decline resets expectations around McDonald's and puts more weight on whether the cash it generates can justify today's valuation.

headlines.title: McDonald’s Stock Offers Up a Juicy Dividend Yield Above 3%, But I Don’t See Many Other Reasons to Buy It
headlines.summary: A stock needs more than an attractive yield to warrant investor interest.

headlines.title: McDonald’s Dividend King Status Is Impressive, but Valuation Still Matters
headlines.summary: McDonald’s Corporation (NYSE:MCD) has earned a reputation for steady dividends thanks to its global network of franchises, strong royalty income, and pricing power. But if you’re investing for income, it’s important to look past the company’s defensive reputation.

description: McDonald's Corporation owns, operates, and franchises restaurants under the McDonald's brand in the United States and internationally. It offers food and beverages, including hamburgers and cheeseburgers, various chicken sandwiches, fries, shakes, frozen desserts, sundaes, soft serve cones, cookies, pies, soft drinks, coffee, and other beverages; and full or limited breakfast, as well as sells various other products during limited-time promotions. The company owns and operates franchised restaurants under various structures, including conventional franchise, developmental license, or affiliate. McDonald's Corporation was founded in 1940 and is based in Chicago, Illinois.
